body:
## Summary
Kp has four ways to apply (the conversational apply route, the quick-apply lead form, inbound lead webhooks and inbound CV intake), and each one files the application with its own hand-written code. The copies have already drifted. On the CV door the profile is filed under the wrong workspace, a repeat CV is not merged, and anonymous applicants are merged into one entry. This card moves the whole filing contract into one module, `app/_lib/application-filing.ts`, and turns the doors into thin callers.

## Description
The registry's golden path for application intake has a section, "One core, many doors", which says the contract lives in one place: file the record, dedupe and merge, record consent, audit the gate and acknowledge. Each surface supplies only its validation, its knockout rules, its copy and its decline mode. Kp half-did this. `lead-intake.ts` is a shared core for the quick form and lead webhooks. The conversational route (649 lines) and `cv-intake.ts` still file on their own. The drift is measurable:

- **Tenant split (defect).** `cv-intake.ts:118` builds the profile without the workspace. For an inbound webhook owned by a non-default team (`channels/inbound/[token]/route.ts:153-162`) and for every simulated CV (`sim/apply-cv/route.ts:72-83`), the entry lands in the team's workspace but its profile lands in the default one. That is the bug `route.ts:513-520` describes and fixed for its own door only. The consequences are the ones named there: the recruiter finds no profile, Match never sees the candidate and the follow-up returns 404.
- **Drop instead of merge (defect).** The CV door never looks up the applicant. It builds and saves a profile, and then `createPipelineEntry`'s dedupe hands back the existing row. The new CV ends up as an orphan profile and the existing stub stays degraded.
- **Anonymous collapse (defect).** `cv-intake.ts:112` plus `applyDedupeKey` produce the key `appl-applicant`, so two nameless, email-less CVs merge. The conversational route forbids exactly this at `route.ts:243-246`.
- **Copies.** The entry-stage rule is written 3 times, the consent block 4 times and the status-link mint twice. Name sanitisation exists on one door only.

`fileApplication(input)` owns the tenant, name sanitisation, the identity order (issued token, then email, then name, then nothing), a profile build that always passes the workspace and locale, the all-or-nothing merge, the entry stage, consent, the status-link mint and ack scheduling. The caller states a `proof` level (`token`, `channel` or `none`), which keeps the capability gate at `route.ts:393-422` as policy instead of scattered code. The profile builder is injectable, so the tests do not spawn Python.

## Flow
1. Write `application-filing.test.ts` with the 7 acceptance cases against a throwaway `KP_DB_PATH` and an injected builder. Confirm cases 1-3 and 7 fail.
2. Extract `fileApplication` from the conversational route's first-apply and proven-merge halves: identity, build, entry, consent, status link and deferred ack.
3. Re-implement `ingestCvApplication` and `intakeLead` as wrappers that keep their exported types. Drop the local consent, stage and status-link helpers.
4. Shrink `route.ts` to validation, the knockout verdict, the proof decision and response copy. Delete the quick route's `safeStatusToken`.
5. Update docs/features/candidates and docs/features/pipeline (the stage table at pipeline/README.md:122 names both helpers).

## Expected impact
Closed: a real multi-workspace defect on the inbound CV channel (entry and profile in different tenants), an orphan-profile leak and a silent merge of strangers. After this, any new door (a referral path, an ATS pull) inherits the whole contract by construction. The conversational route loses about 250 lines.

## Evaluation
Claim: all four doors file through one module that always passes the tenant, resolves identity before building, and never dedupes on the anonymous label.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (the new test file and source guard do not exist; cases 1-3 fail on current behaviour).
After: 7 of 7.
Method: architecture: node:test over app/_lib/application-filing.test.ts plus the unchanged reapply-capability-gate, apply-intake-scope, apply-ack-after-response, inbound-lead, lead-intake-locale and cv-intake-sim-scope suites, then the full integration gate.
Result: pending build.
Gate: architecture

body:
## Summary
A candidate who applies again without their emailed link today reads "It looks like you've already applied ... We've noted your renewed interest" on a card with no action. They lose their status link and any way to update the application, and the renewed interest is never recorded. This card makes the duplicate answer do what the route's own comment promises: re-send the candidate's own status link and enrichment link to the address already on file. The send is rate-limited per entry, is never addressed to whoever typed the request, and writes nothing to the matched entry.

## Description
The capability gate (`route.ts:393-422`, `quick/route.ts:176-200`) was right to stop handing tokens to anyone who types a known name or email. It left the real returning candidate at a dead end, though. The only recovery the code names, "the enrichment link is re-sent to the address on file" (`route.ts:412-414`), does not exist: the branch returns without dispatching anything. Under the registry's `recoverable-decline-and-no-dead-ends` test ("can the candidate reach a submitted application using only the controls in front of them, without a fresh link"), a candidate who lost the ack email fails today. Re-applying is also their only update channel (`merge-dont-drop-on-reapplication`), and that channel needs the lead token they no longer have.

The fix delivers the capability to the one party who can prove ownership, the inbox on record. Nothing new is exposed to the caller:
- `apply-link-recovery.ts` is pure: `decideLinkRecovery({contact, anonymized, throttled, relayConfigured})` returns send, or skip with a reason. `recoveryMessageKey(relayConfigured)` never reads whether a contact exists, so the response cannot be used to probe for an address.
- `dispatchApplicationLinks(entry, {statusLink, enrichLink})` in comms-dispatch reuses the ack's link lines under a "your application links" subject. It is sent through `afterResponse` and writes no pipeline event, so the unproven path stays out of the recruiter's feed, as the existing gate test requires.
- The cooldown is `login-throttle` keyed `apply-links:<entryId>`, 1 per 24h. It is persisted across workers, so a griefer can cause at most one email per day, delivered to the real candidate and containing only that candidate's own links.
- Copy: `alreadyMessage` stops claiming the interest was noted. New `alreadyMessageRecover` and `alreadyMessageNoRelay` keys go into all 4 locales, plus the email subject and intro.

## Flow
1. Write `apply-link-recovery.test.ts` (cases 1-2) and extend `reapply-capability-gate.test.ts` with route-level cases 3-7 (a victim WITH a contact, a repeat inside the cooldown, the quick door, the unchanged event count).
2. Implement the pure module, then `dispatchApplicationLinks` and a status-link mint plus `ensureLeadEnrichToken` on the existing entry.
3. Wire both duplicate branches: conversational `route.ts:415-421` and quick `quick/route.ts:194-200`.
4. Add the catalog keys to all four locales in one locked commit. Update docs/features/candidates (the apply duplicate policy) and docs/features/comms (the new candidate message kind).

## Expected impact
A returning applicant who lost their link gets a working status link and a prefilled update path in their inbox within seconds, instead of a dead end with a false claim. The recruiter stops receiving the third and fourth attempts and the "I applied, did you get it?" emails the technique names as the usual follow-ups. The security posture is unchanged: nothing is returned on the wire and nothing is written to the entry.

## Evaluation
Claim: an unproven duplicate application, on either door, re-sends the entry's own links to the address on file, at most once per 24h per entry, without leaking tokens or contact existence and without writing to the entry.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass.
After: 7 of 7.
Method: contract: node:test over app/_lib/apply-link-recovery.test.ts and the extended app/api/apply/[id]/reapply-capability-gate.test.ts on a throwaway SQLite file, plus i18n:check for 4-locale parity.
Result: pending build.
Gate: contract
